## Summary

<!-- In a short paragraph, usually two to four sentences, explain the
problem in plain English: who or what is affected, what is wrong, missing,
or unnecessarily difficult, and why that matters.

Assume the reader knows what the project does but has not followed this
work. Use familiar words. Leave internal names, unexplained acronyms,
architecture, and implementation details for the sections below. -->

## Why

<!-- Add the evidence, established cause, or constraints that explain the
need for this change. Explain non-obvious choices when they help review it.
Add useful context beyond the Summary instead of repeating it.

Distinguish observed facts from hypotheses. Link relevant issues or
designs, keeping the essential reasoning in the PR. Keep this section
short when the change needs little background. -->

## What changes

<!-- Describe the behavior delivered by this PR, its scope, and meaningful
limits. Use a before/after example when it makes the result clearer.

Distinguish implemented behavior from proposals and deferred work.
Link required companion changes and relevant follow-up issues. -->

## Risks and compatibility

<!-- Describe material compatibility, data, safety, configuration, or
deployment effects. Include required component versions, upgrade ordering,
migration, or recovery guidance where relevant.

If no material risk is expected, briefly explain why that follows from
the scope. -->

## Verification

<!-- Report the checks that actually ran, their observed results, and
which behavior or risk they cover. Include relevant commands, environment
details, test references, or CI links.

Distinguish passed, failed, not run, and not applicable. Explain important
coverage gaps. Keep planned checks separate from completed evidence.

Add manual steps only when they provide useful additional verification.
State the setup, expected result, whether the check was performed, and
cleanup when it changes persistent state. -->
